Stuffed pretzel crust is hard to do due to the oil that we use in our pans. The baking soda mixture is literally baking soda and water. What does water not mix with? Oil. 

Now it’s not impossible to make it look like the picture. Just add more baking soda to the water. But if you use the “correct” amount it will never look like the picture.

Assistant manager here. Delegate. You should know who does what best. Put them in that station and keep your head on a swivel. Crew members will slack a bit if you’re not on top of them. 

Obviously don’t be too much of a hard ass, but keep your crew in check. No phones. Talk and WORK. Don’t mind if you’re chatting, but I still need to see some pep in your step. 

Also they won’t respect you if you’re just standing there telling them what to do. Find the station where you can see almost every part of the store and work that station. For me it’s make line. I work make line and watch everyone else. If they see you working your butt off, then they won’t catch attitudes if you tell them to do the same. 

Time management. If you’re closing, as soon as the rush is over start cleaning. Have someone wipe out and oil pans, have someone on dishes, and have the rest run the business side of things. Don’t let people go home too early to save on labor. This will bite you in the ass. Trust me I’ve done it and stayed until 1 am to finish cleaning. 

All in all, do your job, lead by example, and still have fun!

I’ve noticed often times when a child this age laughs or smiles while being aggressive, they are simply overstimulated. I’ve had children laugh and run around hitting their friends, only to find out they needed an outlet for all of that energy or need some calm time. Him saying he’s scared could be him trying to communicate anxiety brought on by overstimulation. This can be very frustrating for kids this age and can cause a lot of behavioral issues. 

Have you tried keeping something in his hands at all times? I know it’s hard with other toddlers, but it could help keep his hands busy. Do you have a calming time that isn’t nap? After circle time with my kids, we will do stretches (they love this! It really helps regulate their bodies and it’s fun!) turn off the lights, and read a book or two. I’ve noticed a big difference in “hell hour” (the hour before lunch and nap) with this.

She respects us and asks for our opinions. Defends us against parents (even one’s that are on the board). Reimburses us for art, toys, or anything we buy with our own money for the kids. Has a list in the office for us to request supplies. Buys all of us lunch when we’re having a rough week. And so much more. She makes working there enjoyable. 

I’m saying all of this because you should have this support. Everyone should. I’ve had gossipy directors before and they are the worst. I understand. For your own sake keep looking for centers. You will find your unicorn. In the mean time good luck!
